title: STM32L476 HardFault immediately after entering Reset_Handler (before .data initialization)
content:
I'm working on a completely bare-metal STM32L476RG project using GCC + CMake + OpenOCD + GDB (no HAL, no CubeMX).

The MCU consistently HardFaults immediately after entering Reset_Handler, before any .data copy or .bss initialization occurs.

Toolchain

  • MCU: STM32L476RG
  • GCC: arm-none-eabi-gcc 15.2.1
  • OpenOCD + GDB
  • CMake project
  • -mcpu=cortex-m4
  • -mthumb
  • -nostartfiles
 

Linker

Memory layout:

FLASH (rx) : ORIGIN = 0x08000000, LENGTH = 1024K
RAM   (rwx): ORIGIN = 0x20000000, LENGTH = 128K

_estack = ORIGIN(RAM) + LENGTH(RAM);

Relevant symbols:

_sdata  = 0x20000000
_edata  = 0x20000030
_sidata = 0x08000A7C

_sbss   = 0x20000030
_ebss   = 0x20000034
 

Vector table

Vector table begins at 0x08000000.

First entries:

0x20020000   // MSP
0x08000197   // Reset_Handler
0x08000201   // NMI
0x0800018D   // HardFault

Reading both

0x00000000

and

0x08000000

shows identical contents, so the Flash alias appears correct.

VTOR:

0xE000ED08 = 0x00000000
 

Reset_Handler

void Reset_Handler(void)
{
    extern uint32_t _sdata, _edata, _sidata;
    extern uint32_t _sbss, _ebss;

    uint32_t *_sdatap  = &_sdata;
    uint32_t *_edatap  = &_edata;
    uint32_t *_sidatap = &_sidata;

    uint32_t *_sbssp = &_sbss;
    uint32_t *_ebssp = &_ebss;

    while (_sdatap < _edatap)
        *_sdatap++ = *_sidatap++;

    while (_sbssp < _ebssp)
        *_sbssp++ = 0;

    main();

    while (1);
}
 

What GDB shows

Breakpoint at Reset_Handler is hit correctly.

Disassembly:

push {r7, lr}
sub sp, #24
add r7, sp, #0
...

Flash contents at that location match the disassembly exactly.

 

The strange part

Using stepi:

  • push {r7,lr} executes.
  • Immediately afterwards execution enters HardFault_Handler.

We never reach the first ldr instruction.

So the fault appears to occur before any .data or .bss initialization.

 

Fault status registers

HFSR = 0x40000000
CFSR = 0x1400
SHCSR = 0x00000000

0x1400 decodes to:

  • INVSTATE
  • UNDEFINSTR

No BusFault bits are set.

This is confusing because the instruction stream consists only of valid Thumb instructions (push, sub sp,#24, add).

 

HardFault handler

I also tried a naked HardFault handler:

__attribute__((naked))
void HardFault_Handler(void)
{
    __asm volatile(
        "tst lr,#4
"
        "ite eq
"
        "mrseq r0,msp
"
        "mrsne r0,psp
"
        "bkpt #0
");
}

The exception frame pointed to by r0 contains only zeros, which I did not expect.

 

Things I've already verified

  • Reset vector is correct.
  • Vector table contents are correct.
  • Flash programming is correct.
  • Linker symbols match the literal pool in Reset_Handler.
  • MSP starts at 0x20020000.
  • Reset_Handler is definitely entered.
  • CPU is identified correctly (CPUID = 0x410FC241).
  • Project is compiled for Cortex-M4 Thumb (-mcpu=cortex-m4 -mthumb).
 

My question

Has anyone seen a Cortex-M4 HardFault immediately after entering Reset_Handler, before any memory initialization, with CFSR = 0x1400 (INVSTATE + UNDEFINSTR)?

Is there something obvious I'm overlooking, or does this point toward a toolchain/debug configuration issue rather than a startup-code problem?

Below are my startup.c and linker.ld files. I couldnt upload since the site is telling me that they are unsupported file type.
Ive used the same startup.c and linker script before for a previous project and it worked fine. The only changes i’ve made is use the entire memory for the linker script this time and allocate 4 KB for stack and heap each.

void Reset_Handler(void){                            //extern declaration of start,end and ram copy of data as well as of start and end of bss
    extern uint32_t _sdata;
    extern uint32_t _edata; 
    extern uint32_t _sidata;

    extern uint32_t _sbss;
    extern uint32_t _ebss;

    uint32_t *_sdatap = &_sdata;
    uint32_t *_edatap = &_edata;
    uint32_t *_sidatap = &_sidata;

    uint32_t *_sbssp = &_sbss;
    uint32_t *_ebssp = &_ebss;

    while(_sdatap<_edatap){                        //Initializing data variables and zeroing bss variables
        (*_sdatap) = (*_sidatap);
        _sdatap++;
        _sidatap++;
    }

    while(_sbssp<_ebssp){
        (*_sbssp) = 0;
        _sbssp++;
    }

    main();                                        //Calling main

    while(1){                                     //Infinite loop in the event of main somehow returning
    }
}

void Default_Handler(void){
    while(1){};
}

void HardFault_C(uint32_t *stack)
{
    volatile uint32_t r0  = stack[0];
    volatile uint32_t r1  = stack[1];
    volatile uint32_t r2  = stack[2];
    volatile uint32_t r3  = stack[3];
    volatile uint32_t r12 = stack[4];
    volatile uint32_t lr  = stack[5];
    volatile uint32_t pc  = stack[6];
    volatile uint32_t psr = stack[7];

    while (1);
}
ENTRY(Reset_Handler)


_Min_Heap_Size  = 0x1000;   
_Min_Stack_Size = 0x1000;   

MEMORY
{
    FLASH (rx) : ORIGIN = 0x08000000, LENGTH = 1024K
    RAM (rwx)  : ORIGIN = 0x20000000, LENGTH = 128K
}

_estack = ORIGIN(RAM) + LENGTH(RAM);


SECTIONS
{
    .isr_vector :
    {
        . = ALIGN(128);
        KEEP(*(.isr_vector))
    } > FLASH

    .text :
    {
        *(.text*)
        *(.rodata*)
        . = ALIGN(4);
        _etext = .;
    } > FLASH

    .data :
    {
        _sdata = .;
        *(.data*)
        _edata = .;
    } > RAM AT > FLASH

    _sidata = LOADADDR(.data);

    .bss :
    {
        _sbss = .;
        *(.bss*)
        *(COMMON)
        _ebss = .;
    } > RAM
}

scraped_replies.html: Generate a bare CubeMX project and compare. It’ll take 5 minutes. Especially compare the disassembly at Reset_Handler.
You need to load a value into SP before using the stack. Hard to do explicitly in C which is why startup file is written in assembly. Follow the existing startup file examples.
